newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Port of Tauranga cargo volumes up 6.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Port of Tauranga cargo volumes up 6.2 pct.

text.p: Port of Tauranga Ltd said on Monday its higher first-half earnings reflected a 6.2 percent increase in cargo volumes for the period, along with more shipping movements and continued growth in income from company-owned property.
Log exports again dominated the rise in cargo volumes, increasing by 16 percent to 1.72 million tonnes.

Other forestry products, led by wood pulp and paper, also contributed, with growth of five percent. Steel exports rose eight percent, following a 25 percent increase in the same period last year, and dairy product cargoes also grew by 16 percent.
On the import side, oil cargoes rose by 13 percent to 437,600 tonnes.
Income from company-owned property grew by 13.8 percent.
"The company's financial position has strengthened further with shareholders' equity increasing to 65.9 percent and term debt cut to $48.34 million," Chairman Fraser McKenzie said.
The board expects to appoint a new chief executive by the end of March following the retirement of John Halling.
Negotiations with customers over a revised tariff structure were currently being completed, with new tariffs to be phased in over a period of time.

Port of Tauranga earlier reported a rise in net profit for the six months to December 31 to NZ$5.28 million from $4.42 million a year earlier. It declared a fully imputed dividend of 3.5 cents, up from 2.4 cents a year ago.
